title: Snapshot Prefetch Gateway and Graceful KV Warmup Orchestration
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Problem: Dedicated customer fleets observe long tail cold starts when tenants attach after idle periods. Current warm-pool strategies focus on full weight residency or naive KV seeding which either wastes GPU memory or fails to reduce first-request latency for large-context workloads.

Goal: Implement a Snapshot Prefetch Gateway (SPG) that orchestrates lightweight parameter snapshot fetches and a graceful KV warmup flow that stages KV population by access heat. The SPG will act as a policy-driven admission point for incoming attach/scale events and coordinate non-blocking prefetches to reduce P50 and P95 cold-start token latency while bounding memory and network egress.

Scope: Dedicated capacity fleets only (reserved GPU pools). Work includes admission policy, snapshot packaging format, prefetch orchestration, KV warmup throttling and decay, observability hooks, and a controlled rollout path. This does NOT modify tenant billing or allocation logic in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: SPG deployed behind fleet control plane and accepts attach events with policy-based prefetch directives
Median (P50) first-token latency for cold attaches reduced by >= 30% on benchmark trace (internal synthetic large-context workload)
P95 first-token latency reduced by >= 20% without increasing steady-state memory usage by more than 8% on a 100-tenant synthetic cluster
KV warmup is non-blocking: requests that miss warmed keys proceed with fallback and observe graceful degradation instead of hard stalls
Telemetry: per-attach timeline tracing available in Console (prefetch start/end, bytes transferred, warm steps completed)
technical_notes: Snapshot format: delta-compressed shard snapshots (fingerprint + chunk manifest) to allow small initial streaming bursts
Admission policies: priority, SLA tier, recent-traffic score, and predictive-hit probability derived from recent routing histograms
KV warmup stages: 1) fingerprint probe (small KV checks), 2) hot-key prefetch (top-1% predicted keys), 3) streaming background fill for remaining working set
Backpressure: SPG exposes token-bucket egress budgets per-tenant and global concurrency limiter to bound cold-start impact
Safety: snapshot verification via checksum + signing (existing KMS flow reused), prefetch failures are retried with exponential backoff and do not block attach completion
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal canary on a 3-node dedicated pool with synthetic traces (2 weeks)
Beta: enable SPG for 5 low-traffic customers with opt-in flag (4 weeks)
Gradual rollout: increase concurrency and tenant coverage while monitoring P95 SLOs and egress budgets (metric gating)
Fallback: feature-flagged global kill switch and automatic disable if P95 regression > 10% or egress > configured budget
testing_steps: Run synthetic attach traces (varied context lengths) against baseline and SPG-enabled cluster; collect first-token latency and steady-state memory
Fault injection: drop snapshot chunks mid-stream to verify retry and graceful fallback to on-demand load
Chaos test: simulate network saturation to ensure admission policy throttles prefetches and keeps tails bounded
End-to-end: create a dedicated fleet, attach 50 tenants with staggered traffic, observe Console timelines and logs
metrics: prefetch_egress_bytes per-attach: keep within budget threshold
kv_warm_completion_rate: % of attaches finishing hot-key stage within 10s
comments: 2026-03-02 - Priya Desai: Spike complete. Snapshot delta layers reduce initial fetch size by ~65% on our 2B-parameter test model. Network egress is the dominant cost; need a policy to gate prefetches.
